sourceInformation.genre: Surgical action; visual-novel drama; cooperative arcade simulation
sourceInformation.perspective: Fixed surgeon-eye 3D operative field with mild perspective; frontal paper theatre for story
sourceInformation.tech: Pavilion engine 0.1.0 at 49ef2ba, Rust 1.98.1, WebAssembly, wgpu 30, glam 0.33, wasm-bindgen 0.2.129; HTML/CSS/JavaScript shell and Web Audio
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original procedural cel-shaded medical illustrations, steel instruments, teal drapes, violet organisms, extruded paper characters; Barlow Condensed Semibold
sourceInformation.animation: Pavilion sim-driven procedural animation: heartbeat tissue, articulated instruments, spline-card acting, parasites, particles and score stamps
sourceInformation.audio: Original synthesized melodies, heartbeat-coupled score, procedural effects and Animalese-style formant voices; music defaults to 10%; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1 shared-world Code Blue for 1–4 players, host authority, mirrored snapshots, local controller co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Rust and WASM campaign, gestures, controller/touch stand-ins, audio analyser, saves, checkpoints, UI bounds, AI Hub harness and two-copy synchronization; 24 responsive captures in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Real WebGPU art checked in Chromium. WebKit checks its requirement message; real iOS Safari, physical controllers, a second human and listening review were unavailable.
sourceInformation.research: Research supplied by PLAN.md on the 2006 Wii source; read Pavilion START_HERE.md, MAKE_A_GAME.md and engine APIs, and the full AI Hub protocol

testingFeedback: Testing caught four product issues: idle-controller input arbitration, touch-attract exit, chart contrast and overflowing panels. Additional checks guard idle-player AI assistance and touch-keyboard transitions. Two test assertions also needed correction.
Two were game breaking for affected inputs or screens: an idle pad could overwrite mouse/keyboard actions, and low-contrast charts hid essential briefing text.
Real mouse and controller gesture tests with both connected. They found an input failure the deterministic bot could not expose; the full campaign test separately proved feature coverage.
Repeating identical deterministic bot case runs added little after snapshots and replays had been verified.
engineFeedback: The deterministic Game hook, snapshots and cel-shaded WebGPU renderer made a new genre testable and gave surgical instruments useful lighting and shadows.

The stock application owns demo menus, camera controls and touch input. I used a dedicated product host rather than trying to adapt that flow. Adding frame/input fields also required updating other constructors.
The physical gesture evaluator and replayable four-surgeon state: tracing, extraction axes, stitch crossings, timed heat and doses, gifts and resuscitation.
Custom game presentation required reading RenderFrame, ViewBuilder, CameraRig, Renderer and input-tool internals. UI, camera, audio and rendering have separate integration points.

Registered surgery; extended InputFrame and RenderFrame; added the procedural surgery view, extruded paper actors, a native surgical input command and a dedicated wasm host. The original renderer and sim-driven animation remain the base; the browser shell and synthesized audio use HTML and Web Audio.
A documented per-game product interface owning camera, input, UI, audio and custom scene emission would remove much of the integration work.
promptFeedback: The combination of a distinctive source-inspired design, explicit delivery format and editable-data requirement gave the game a clear identity and finish line.
The plan describes an hour-long campaign while the task asks for a vertical slice. Its permission to shorten waves made the scope practical without dropping mechanics.
Making mouse gestures, controller precision, the heartbeat clock, story pacing and shared-world co-op work together as one game.
Keep the concrete deliverables and testing rules; distinguish required demo mechanics from suggested campaign length, and provide a small custom-product engine host example.

aiHub.name: Trauma Refrain: Third Opinion
aiHub.description: A surgical-action drama in a rain-soaked harbour hospital. Trace, pull, stitch and cauterize through eight cases, then fight a man-made parasite that keeps time with the heart.
aiHub.controls: Right stick or mouse aims; R2, left click or E operates; left stick flick or 1–8 selects tools; Space/Triangle gifts; Esc/Options pauses.
